 المواسير المسدودة

 التى بها تهريب

 او انسداد

sections_en.text: The first draft of the document was prepared by Eng. Ahmed Sayed Hussein, tested by Eng. Sayed Mohamed Ahmed, accepted by Eng. Abdel Azim Hagras, General Manager, approved by Eng. Hussein Ahmed El-Mahdy, Head of the Stations Sector, and certified by Eng. Gamal Abdel Wahab, MPIS coordinator and Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at the Upper Egypt Electricity Production Company.
Technical information for the gland steam condenser
- Number of tubes (139), stainless steel, number of passes (4)
- Tube length (1600 mm), inside diameter (12 mm), outside diameter (14 mm)

rows: Make sure the unit to be worked on is isolated.
Issue an approved work order from the competent authority; the maintenance team must hold an occupational safety and health category card.
Record the names of the workers on the work order and their occupational safety and health categories.
Cordon off the work area and place the appropriate warning signs.
Workers must wear occupational safety and health tools while carrying out the work, such as helmet, gloves, masks and protective shoes.
Hammer, drift punch of two different diameters.
Grinder, sandpaper.
Replacement tubes with the same specifications as the new tubes.
Large set of wooden plugs (dowels).
Rod for cleaning (rodding rod).
Disconnect the cooling water and steam inlet and outlet connections.
Remove the condenser cover from the top.
Remove the condenser flange from the bottom.
Take out the condenser and load it horizontally on the stand for testing.
Test the condenser tubes by inserting the cleaning rod into all the tubes to identify the blocked tubes.
Test the unblocked tubes by closing one side with wooden plugs and pushing water under pressure from the other side, thus identifying the tubes with leakage.
Using the drift punch and hammer, remove the tubes with leakage or blockage.
Fit the new tubes and expand them at their ends.
Test the new tubes as in step (6).
Return the condenser to its vertical position on the base, and fit the upper cover of the condenser.
Tighten the flanges for the cooling water and steam inlet and outlet.
Open the cooling water inlet valve to put the condenser in service.

Introduction
The first draft of the document was prepared by Eng. Ahmed Sayed Hussein, tested by Eng. Sayed Mohamed Ahmed, accepted by Eng. Abdel Azim Hagras, General Manager, approved by Eng. Hussein Ahmed El-Mahdy, Head of the Stations Sector, and certified by Eng. Gamal Abdel Wahab, MPIS coordinator and Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at the Upper Egypt Electricity Production Company.
Technical information for the gland steam condenser
- Number of tubes (139), stainless steel, number of passes (4)
- Tube length (1600 mm), inside diameter (12 mm), outside diameter (14 mm)
Safety Precautions
Make sure the unit to be worked on is isolated.
Issue an approved work order from the competent authority; the maintenance team must hold an occupational safety and health category card.
Record the names of the workers on the work order and their occupational safety and health categories.
Cordon off the work area and place the appropriate warning signs.
Workers must wear occupational safety and health tools while carrying out the work, such as helmet, gloves, masks and protective shoes.
Tools, Equipment and Instruments Used
Hammer, drift punch of two different diameters.
Grinder, sandpaper.
Replacement tubes with the same specifications as the new tubes.
Large set of wooden plugs (dowels).
Rod for cleaning (rodding rod).
Procedures to be Carried Out
Disconnect the cooling water and steam inlet and outlet connections. | 1.
Remove the condenser cover from the top. | 2.
Remove the condenser flange from the bottom. | 3.
Take out the condenser and load it horizontally on the stand for testing. | 4.
Test the condenser tubes by inserting the cleaning rod into all the tubes to identify the blocked tubes. | 5.
Test the unblocked tubes by closing one side with wooden plugs and pushing water under pressure from the other side, thus identifying the tubes with leakage. | 6.
Using the drift punch and hammer, remove the tubes with leakage or blockage. | 7.
Fit the new tubes and expand them at their ends. | 8.
Test the new tubes as in step (6). | 9.
Return the condenser to its vertical position on the base, and fit the upper cover of the condenser. | 10.
Tighten the flanges for the cooling water and steam inlet and outlet. | 11.
Open the cooling water inlet valve to put the condenser in service. | 12.
